title: The Midnight Vendor
briefing: Bluefin Bakery is missing $48,750. Every payment went to ‘Northshore Supply’, a vendor that doesn’t exist. And every payment went out at exactly 11:52 PM.

suspects.name: Sam Okafor
suspects.public_bio: Keeps the books. Knows where every dollar should be.
suspects.opening: H-hello? Yes, this is Sam. I’ve been going over the accounts all morning. Something is very wrong.

private.alibi: At a job interview at a competing bakery last Tuesday, home at night.
private.secret: Secretly interviewing for a job with a competitor.
private.red_herring_reason: Afraid the bakery will fire him for job hunting.
knows: Northshore payments all went out at 11:52 PM
His job interview was Tuesday afternoon
private.personality: Polite, anxious, helpful. Says ‘yes, sending it right away’.
private.breaking_point: Admits the job interview when asked about Tuesday twice.

suspects.name: Marcus Bell
suspects.public_bio: First one in. Last one out. Usually.
suspects.opening: Marcus here. Look, if this is about that night at the bakery… I can explain why I was there.

private.alibi: At the bakery late, trying to fix a dent in the delivery van.
private.secret: Dented the delivery van and tried to fix it without telling the manager.
private.red_herring_reason: Does not want to pay for the van repair.
knows: Priya’s office light was on around midnight
He saw her silhouette through the office window
He was fixing the delivery van
private.breaking_point: Admits the van damage when questioned about being there.

questions: What did you see that night?
Why did you stay after hours?

suspects.name: Priya Nair
suspects.public_bio: Runs a tight ship. Nothing happens without her say-so.
suspects.opening: Detective. I’m glad someone is taking this seriously. Sam handles the books; I’d start with him.

private.alibi: Claims she is always home asleep by 10 PM.
private.secret: Created Northshore Supply as a shell vendor, then scheduled three payments from her login at 11:52 PM.
knows: She was in the office at 11:52 PM
private.personality: Composed, exact, subtly controlling. Blames Sam without sounding hostile.
private.breaking_point: Only folds after both transaction_sheet and eyewitness have been presented to her, or both clues are unlocked and Marcus confronts her in cross-examination.

questions: What do you know about Northshore?

suspects.name: Elena Ruiz
suspects.public_bio: Built the bakery. Has everything to lose.
suspects.opening: Detective. Forty-eight thousand dollars… that’s months of payroll. Please tell me you can find it.
questions: Who could approve a new vendor?
What are you keeping from the staff?

private.alibi: At home with her daughter. Returned at 6 AM to open the bakery.
private.secret: Used her own savings to cover overdue rent without telling the staff.
private.red_herring_reason: Fears everyone will leave if they learn the bakery is struggling.
knows: She covered the rent from personal savings
She does not recognize Northshore Supply
Sam reconciles the ledger, but operations manages vendor setup
private.personality: Tired, protective, occasionally sharp, afraid for her staff.
private.breaking_point: Admits the rent problem when asked what she is hiding.

suspects.name: Theo Park
suspects.public_bio: Has the passwords. Keeps his own hours.
suspects.opening: Theo. I maintain the network. Before you ask: having administrator access doesn’t mean I move money.
questions: Were you logged in that night?
Could someone use another person’s login?

private.alibi: Finished his remote maintenance session at 9:10 PM, then worked on a personal freelance project at home.
private.secret: Used the bakery’s spare server for a freelance project without permission.
private.red_herring_reason: Worries he will lose his contract for misusing the server.
knows: His maintenance session ended at 9:10 PM
A network administrator cannot approve banking purchases
Staff are supposed to use individual banking credentials
private.personality: Dry, technically precise, a little defensive; becomes warmer once trusted.
private.breaking_point: Admits the unauthorized freelance project if challenged about server use.

evidence.title: The transaction sheet
evidence.summary: Three payments. One vendor. Exactly the same time.

note.text: Three transfers to Northshore Supply. $48,750 total. Every one at 11:52 PM.

evidence.annotation: Same vendor. Same minute. Every time.

evidence.title: A light after midnight
evidence.summary: Marcus saw a light in Priya’s office around midnight.

note.text: Marcus saw Priya’s office light on around midnight. Ask her where she was.

evidence.statement: The night I was there, Priya’s office light was on around midnight. I saw her silhouette through the window. I was outside fixing the van.

hints: Money has a clock. Check when it moved.
Put the witness and the manager in the same room.

truth_timeline.title: A vendor with no business
truth_timeline.event: Priya creates Northshore Supply, a shell vendor with no deliveries and no real inventory.

truth_timeline.title: The first payment
truth_timeline.event: $16,250 leaves Bluefin Bakery. Priya is in her office. Outside, Marcus is quietly repairing a dent in the delivery van.

truth_timeline.title: Same minute. Same scheme.
truth_timeline.event: Two more payments of $16,250 follow. Three transactions total $48,750, all sent to Northshore Supply.

truth_timeline.title: The books don’t balance
truth_timeline.event: Sam finds the missing money. His nervousness was about a job interview, not the theft. Marcus’s eyewitness account breaks Priya’s alibi. Elena was hiding rent trouble; Theo was concealing an unauthorized freelance project. Neither moved the missing money.

cliffhanger: I only set up the vendor… someone else approved every payment.

next_mission.title: The Second Signature
next_mission.description: Three approvals. One unfamiliar signature. The trail doesn’t end at Bluefin Bakery.

opening_letter.subject: The payroll money is gone.
paragraphs: I need your help. $48,750 has disappeared from Bluefin Bakery’s accounts. That’s months of payroll for the people who keep this place alive.
Every payment went to “Northshore Supply.” We have no supplier by that name. And every transfer was made at exactly 11:52 PM.
I’ve given you five contacts who may know something. Speak to them. Ask for records. Find out where the money went—and who sent it.
Please find the truth before we lose the bakery.

tagline: $48,750 vanished from a small bakery. Every payment left at 11:52 PM.
